[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply **BODMAS**: Solve the **bracket** first, then **multiplication**, then **addition**/**subtraction**.

⇒ (25 + 19) = 44

⇒ 44 × 2 = 88

⇒ 71 + 56 − 88 + 92 − 38 = (71 + 56 + 92) − (88 + 38) = 219 − 126 = 93

**∴ The correct answer is 93.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 71 + 56 − (25 + 19) × 2 + 92 − 38

**Rule Used:** **BODMAS** (Bracket, Order, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 71 + 56 − (44) × 2 + 92 − 38 (Solving **Bracket**)

⇒ 71 + 56 − 88 + 92 − 38 (Performing **Multiplication**)

⇒ 127 − 88 + 92 − 38 (Performing **Addition** from left to right)

⇒ 39 + 92 − 38

⇒ 131 − 38

⇒ 93

**∴ The correct answer is 93.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule Hierarchy

Operations must follow the order: **Brackets** ((), {}, []), **Orders** (powers, square roots), **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Sign Convention for Grouping

To avoid mistakes in large expressions, group all **positive terms** and **negative terms** separately before the final subtraction.

Multiplication Priority

Always ensure that a **multiplication** operation (like 44 × 2) is completed before any **addition** or **subtraction** that surrounds it.

questions.question: 89 + 33 - (27 of 2) + 44 ÷ 4 + 18 of 2 - 36 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **BODMAS** rule to solve the expression efficiently.

Solve **Of** and **Brackets** first: (27 of 2) = 54 and 18 of 2 = 36.

Next, perform **Division**: 44 ÷ 4 = 11.

Simplify the expression by canceling out +36 and −36: 89 + 33 − 54 + 11 + 0.

Final calculation: 122 − 54 + 11 = 68 + 11 = 79.

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 89 + 33 − (27 of 2) + 44 ÷ 4 + 18 of 2 − 36

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS** (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 89 + 33 − 54 + 44 ÷ 4 + 36 − 36 (Solving **Bracket** and **Of** operations)

⇒ 89 + 33 − 54 + 11 + 36 − 36 (Performing **Division**: 44 ÷ 4 = 11)

⇒ 122 − 54 + 11 + 0 (Solving **Addition**: 89 + 33 = 122 and 36 − 36 = 0)

⇒ 68 + 11 (Solving **Subtraction**: 122 − 54 = 68)

⇒ 79

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It stands for **Bracket** (), **Of** (multiplication), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

The 'Of' Operator

In simplification, **Of** indicates multiplication and must be calculated before division and regular multiplication.

Left-to-Right Priority

When operations of the same priority (like addition and subtraction) remain, solve them from **left to right** for accuracy.

questions.question: Two numbers have a sum of 156 and an HCF of 13. If their LCM is 455, find the numbers.
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Identify the pair in the options that satisfies the **sum = 156**. Option 1: 13 + 39 = 52 | Option 2: **65 + 91 = 156** Option 3: 39 + 65 = 104 | Option 4: 78 + 91 = 169 Only **65 and 91** satisfy the sum condition; also their **LCM is 455** (13 × 5 × 7). **∴ The correct answer is 65 and 91.**

questions.question: (frac{sqrt{0.0169}}{1.3}) times ((0.18)/(sqrt{3.24)}) times ((0.24)/(sqrt{0.0576)}) = ?

Substitute the roots back into the given expression: (0.13 ÷ 1.3) × (0.18 ÷ 1.8) × (0.24 ÷ 0.24). The calculation reduces to 0.1 × 0.1 × 1 = 0.01. **∴ The correct answer is 0.01.**

questions.question: If x = sqrt{169} times sqrt{81} times sqrt{121} , then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **unit digit** of each square root: √169 ends in 3, √81 ends in 9, and √121 ends in 1.

Multiply the unit digits: 3 × 9 × 1 = 27.

The final result must have **7** as its unit digit.

Comparing with the options, only **1287** ends with the digit 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 1287.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x = √169 × √81 × √121

**Formula Used:** Square root calculation and basic multiplication.

⇒ √169 = 13 (since 13 × 13 = 169)

⇒ √81 = 9 (since 9 × 9 = 81)

⇒ √121 = 11 (since 11 × 11 = 121)

⇒ x = 13 × 9 × 11

⇒ x = 117 × 11

⇒ x = 1287

**∴ The correct answer is 1287.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Squares

A **perfect square** is a number that can be expressed as the product of an integer with itself. For exam speed, memorize squares from 1 to 30.

Multiplication by 11 Shortcut

To multiply a number by 11, such as 117 × 11, write down the last digit (7), add adjacent digits (7+1=8, 1+1=2), and write the first digit (1) to get **1287**.

Square Root Properties

The property √(a × b) = √a × √b allows for the simplification of products involving multiple square roots independently.

questions.question: The area of a rectangle is 54 square cm. The length of the rectangle is 9 cm. What is the ratio of length and breadth of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Breadth** = **Area** ÷ **Length** = 54 ÷ 9 = 6 cm

Required **Ratio** (Length : Breadth) = 9 : 6 = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Area** of the **Rectangle** = 54 cm²

**Length** of the **Rectangle** = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Area** of **Rectangle** = **Length** × **Breadth**

**Ratio** = **Length** : **Breadth**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f794674be577a29cc125f0c9219f4dc62bfba0f05ee2781f72d07708d21ff82d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 54 = 9 × **Breadth**

⇒ **Breadth** = 54 ÷ 9

⇒ **Breadth** = 6 cm

⇒ **Ratio** = **Length** : **Breadth**

⇒ **Ratio** = 9 : 6

⇒ **Ratio** = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The total distance around the boundary of a **rectangle** is calculated using the formula: P = 2 × (length + breadth).

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The **diagonal** (d) of a **rectangle** is the distance between opposite vertices: d = √(length² + breadth²).

Properties of Rectangle

A **rectangle** is a **parallelogram** where all four internal angles are right angles (90°) and opposite sides are equal and parallel.

questions.question: What is the smallest 4-digit number that is divisible by 17?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Smallest 4-digit number = **1000**.

Divide 1000 by 17 → 1000 = (17 × 58) + **14** (Remainder).

To find the next multiple: 1000 + (17 − 14) = **1003**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1003.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisor = **17**, Required number = **Smallest 4-digit number**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7327edfdadb752731c9b314acaccddeb73b8550b1105ca609906e003d3dd130b.png] 

⇒ Smallest 4-digit number = **1000**

⇒ Divide 1000 by 17:

⇒ 1000 = 17 × **58** + **14**

⇒ The smallest 4-digit number divisible by 17 must be the multiple just after 986.

⇒ Next Multiple = 17 × 59

⇒ 17 × (60 − 1) = 1020 − 17

⇒ Required number = **1003**

**∴ The correct answer is 1003.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule for 17

To check if a number is divisible by **17**, subtract 5 times the last digit from the remaining truncated number. Repeat if necessary. Example: 1003 → 100 − (5 × 3) = 85, which is 17 × 5.

General Formula for Smallest n-digit Multiplier

Smallest n-digit number divisible by **x** = (Smallest n-digit number) + (**x** − Remainder), where Remainder is obtained by dividing the smallest n-digit number by **x**.

Largest n-digit Multiplier

Largest n-digit number divisible by **x** = (Largest n-digit number) − (Remainder obtained by dividing it by **x**).

questions.question: ((3.452)² - (2.948)²)/(0.504) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **algebraic identity**: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

Let a = 3.452 and b = 2.948.

Calculate the **difference**: (a − b) = 3.452 − 2.948 = 0.504, which is equal to the **denominator**.

The expression simplifies to (a + b) × (a − b) ÷ (a − b) = a + b.

Required value = 3.452 + 2.948 = 6.4.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numerator = (3.452)² − (2.948)²

Denominator = 0.504

**Formula Used:**

The **difference of squares** formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let a = 3.452 and b = 2.948

⇒ a + b = 3.452 + 2.948 = 6.400

⇒ a − b = 3.452 − 2.948 = 0.504

⇒ Numerator = 6.4 × 0.504

⇒ Expression = (6.4 × 0.504) ÷ 0.504

⇒ Expression = 6.4

**∴ The correct answer is 6.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Two Squares

The expression a² − b² can always be factored into (a − b)(a + b).

Perfect Square Trinomial (Sum)

The square of a sum is given by (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².

Perfect Square Trinomial (Difference)

The square of a difference is given by (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 60 cm. The length of the rectangle is 4 times of its breadth. What is the length (in cm) of its diagonal?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **Length** (L) and **Breadth** (B) = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm.

Ratio L : B = 4 : 1 ⇒ Total 5 units = 30 cm ⇒ 1 unit = 6 cm.

Actual dimensions: L = 24 cm and B = 6 cm.

**Diagonal** = √(24² + 6²) = 6 × √(4² + 1²) = 6√17 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6√17 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Perimeter** of **rectangle** = 60 cm, **Length** (L) = 4 × **Breadth** (B).

**Formula Used:** **Perimeter** = 2(L + B); **Diagonal** = √(L² + B²).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2be06acfc953825093fafecad73bce937d5c259236f77c21ae8a7af6a4af5e6f.png] 

⇒ 2(L + B) = 60

⇒ L + B = 30

⇒ Since L = 4B, 4B + B = 30

⇒ 5B = 30 ⇒ **Breadth** (B) = 6 cm

⇒ **Length** (L) = 4 × 6 = 24 cm

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(24² + 6²)

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(576 + 36) = √612

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(36 × 17) = 6√17 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6√17 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The **diagonal** of a **rectangle** forms the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with the **length** and **breadth**: d = √(l² + b²).

Area of a Rectangle

The total space occupied by the **rectangle** is given by **Area** = Length × Breadth (l × b).

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets of integers that satisfy a² + b² = c², such as (3, 4, 5) or (5, 12, 13), help in quick calculation of **diagonals**.

questions.question: The average weight of A, B and C is 30 kg. The average weight of A and B is 34 kg. The average weight of B and C is 28 kg. What is the weight (in kg) of B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total weight (A+B+C) = 30 × 3 = 90 kg

Total of sub-groups (A+B) and (B+C) = (34 × 2) + (28 × 2) = 68 + 56 = 124 kg

Since **B** is common to both sub-groups, its weight is the difference between the combined sub-groups and the total sum.

Weight of B = 124 − 90 = 34 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 34 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__</st

questions.question: Average of 8 numbers is 30. One of these numbers is 20. 20 is replaced with a new number. New average becomes 42. What is that new number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net increase in the **average** = 42 − 30 = 12

Total increase in **sum** = Increase in average × Total numbers = 12 × 8 = 96

New **number** = Replaced number + Total increase = 20 + 96 = 116

**∴ The correct answer is 116.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of observations = 8

Original **average** = 30

Replaced **number** = 20

New **average** = 42

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = Average × Number of observations

New Number = New Total Sum − (Original Total Sum − Replaced Number)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ffbd0d6eeea92ca6925f16e5e722335f3c637aff3aba2af362d6154d3df3747.png] 

⇒ Original **total sum** = 8 × 30 = 240

⇒ Sum of the other **7 numbers** = 240 − 20 = 220

⇒ New **total sum** = 8 × 42 = 336

⇒ New **number** = 336 − 220 = 116

**∴ The correct answer is 116.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The average or mean is the sum of all values divided by the total count. Formula: Average = (∑xᵢ) ÷ n.

Replacement Rule

When one value is replaced, the change in average is equal to (New Value − Old Value) ÷ Total Count.

Scaling Property

If every number in a data set is increased or decreased by a constant value k, the average also increases or decreases by k.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 3 : 7 and their Highest Common Factor is 5. What are the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is the common multiplier between terms of a **ratio**.

Numbers = (Ratio Parts) × **HCF**

First number = 3 × 5 = 15

Second number = 7 × 5 = 35

**∴ The correct answer is 15, 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of numbers = 3 : 7

**HCF** = 5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32717d262c4f6a7254cb5ca8059f1eac73408153b0bb281e81565d31898d79f8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 3x and 7x, where x is a **common factor**.

⇒ Since 3 and 7 are **co-prime** (no common factor other than 1), the **HCF** of 3x and 7x is x.

⇒ From the question, HCF = 5, so x = 5.

⇒ First number = 3x = 3 × 5 = 15.

⇒ Second number = 7x = 7 × 5 = 35.

**∴ The correct answer is 15, 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Relation

For any two numbers, Product of numbers = HCF × LCM.

LCM from Ratio and HCF

If the ratio of two numbers is a : b and their HCF is h, then their Least Common Multiple (LCM) = a × b × h.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called co-prime if their HCF is 1. All prime numbers are co-prime to each other.

questions.question: Element A is 18 percent by weight in a mixture. How much mixture is required to obtain 90 kg of element A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **mixture**, 18% weight represents the weight of **Element A**.

Given that 18% = 90 kg

⇒ 1% = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 kg

⇒ 100% (Total weight) = 5 × 100 = 500 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 500 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Weight of **Element A** in the mixture = 90 kg

⇒ Percentage of **Element A** by weight = 18%

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Weight = (Weight of component ÷ Percentage of component) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/74b112b2459b6a3f5378ab622b30e611408b89b204676770daae5ff1c0cb7d67.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the total weight of the **mixture** be 'W' kg.

⇒ 18% of W = 90

⇒ (18 ÷ 100) × W = 90

⇒ W = (90 × 100) ÷ 18

⇒ W = 5 × 100

⇒ W = 500 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 500 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Value Conversion

To find the value of a percentage of a total: Value = (Total × Percentage) ÷ 100.

Finding the Base Value

If x% of a number is 'A', then the number itself (100%) is calculated as (A ÷ x) × 100.

Successive Percentage

If a value increases by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by [a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

questions.question: An article is sold for a profit of Rs. 50. Profit percentage is 20 percent. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit percentage 20% corresponds to 1/5 in fraction form.

If 1 unit (Profit) = ₹50

Then 5 units (Cost Price) = 5 × ₹50 = ₹250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Profit = ₹50, Profit Percentage = 20%

**Formula Used:** Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f990b67acb99b81d981c5d895215d164fa82bbb0a34d7feec7884fe52b5d429.png] 

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

⇒ 20 = (50 ÷ Cost Price) × 100

⇒ Cost Price = (50 × 100) ÷ 20

⇒ Cost Price = 50 × 5

⇒ Cost Price = ₹250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Selling Price (SP)

Selling price is the sum of Cost Price and Profit. SP = CP × (100 + Profit %)/100.

Loss Percentage

When CP is greater than SP, a loss occurs. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100, where Loss = CP − SP.

Marked Price (MP)

The price displayed on the article. Discount is always calculated on the MP: SP = MP − Discount.

questions.question: A person sells an article at the profit of 60 percent. Cost price and selling price are increased by 30 percent and 'y' percent respectively. If the new profit percentage is 40 percent, then what is the value of 'y'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume initial **Cost Price (CP)** = 100 → **Initial SP** = 160.

New CP (30% increase) = 130.

New SP with 40% profit = 130 × 1.4 = 182.

Increase in SP (y%) = [(182 − 160) ÷ 160] × 100 = (22 ÷ 160) × 100 = 13.75%.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **Profit** = 60%, **CP increase** = 30%, New **Profit** = 40%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5260907ab4a86f53be0e8569413ef3245524eaa039a2b98ffec72e413610a54.png] 

⇒ Let **Initial CP** = 100

⇒ **Initial SP** = CP + 60% of CP = 100 + 60 = 160

⇒ **New CP** = 100 + 30% of 100 = 130

⇒ **New Profit** = 40%

⇒ **New SP** = 130 + 40% of 130 = 130 + 52 = 182

⇒ Percentage increase in SP (**y**) = [(New SP − Old SP) ÷ Old SP] × 100

⇒ y = [(182 − 160) ÷ 160] × 100

⇒ y = (22 ÷ 160) × 100 = 13.75

**∴ The correct answer is 13.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. It is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value increases by a% and then by b%, the net change is [a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100] %.

Relation between CP and SP

SP = CP × [(100 + Profit %) ÷ 100] or SP = CP × [(100 − Loss %) ÷ 100].

questions.question: A person spends 50 percent of his income. His income increases by 40 percent and his saving increases by 20 percent. What will be the percentage increase in the expenditure?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Assume initial **Income** = 100, then **Expenditure** = 50 and **Saving** = 50. Net change: Total increase in **Income** = 40% of 100 = 40 units. Increase in **Saving** = 20% of 50 = 10 units. Required increase in **Expenditure** = 40 − 10 = 30 units. % Increase in **Expenditure** = (30 ÷ 50) × 100 = 60 percent. **∴ The correct answer is 60 percent.**

questions.question: A pipe can empty 1/3 part of a tank in 45 minutes. In how much time (in minutes) will it empty the complete tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If 1/3rd of the **tank** is emptied in 45 min,

The **complete tank** (1 unit) will be emptied in 45 × 3 min.

Total time = 135 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 135 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Part of **tank** emptied by the **pipe** = 1/3

Time taken to empty 1/3 part = 45 min

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7217371559e246d5641252d9ff36fad689fbc0a90eed1609cc5d0341639a8f1c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total capacity of the **tank** be 1 unit.

⇒ Time to empty 1/3 unit = 45 min

⇒ Time to empty 1 unit = 45 ÷ (1/3)

⇒ Time to empty 1 unit = 45 × 3

⇒ Total time = 135 min

**∴ The correct answer is 135 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method in Time and Work

If a part 'x' of a task is completed in time 'T', then the **total time** to complete the entire task is T ÷ x.

Efficiency of a Pipe

The **efficiency** of an emptying **pipe** is usually taken as negative in combined work problems. Efficiency = Work done ÷ Time taken.

Fractional Work Rule

If a **pipe** empties the **tank** in 'H' hours, then the part emptied in 1 minute is 1 ÷ (60 × H).

questions.question: 6 men can complete a work in 18 days. 8 women can complete the same work in 12 days. 5 boys can complete the same work in 20 days. 10 boys, 12 men and 16 women together can complete the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Work rate of **12 men** = 12 ÷ (6 × 18) = 12 ÷ 108 = 1/9

Work rate of **16 women** = 16 ÷ (8 × 12) = 16 ÷ 96 = 1/6

Work rate of **10 boys** = 10 ÷ (5 × 20) = 10 ÷ 100 = 1/10

Combined efficiency = 1/9 + 1/6 + 1/10 = (20 + 30 + 18) ÷ 180 = 68/180 = 17/45

Required time = Inverse of efficiency = 45/17 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 45/17 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

6 men = 18 days, 8 women = 12 days, 5 boys = 20 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 

 **Person/Group**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 6 Men

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **1 man** = 10 ÷ 6 = 5/3 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of **1 woman** = 15 ÷ 8 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of **1 boy** = 9 ÷ 5 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of (**12 men** + **16 women** + **10 boys**) = 12 × (5/3) + 16 × (15/8) + 10 × (9/5)

⇒ Total combined efficiency = 20 + 30 + 18 = 68 units/day

⇒ Time required = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency = 180 ÷ 68 = 45/17 days

**∴ The correct answer is 45/17 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the efficiency ratio is a:b, the time ratio is b:a.

Work Equivalence Formula

M₁D₁E₁ = M₂D₂E₂, where M is the number of people, D is days, and E is individual efficiency.

Total Work Calculation

Total work is usually considered as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the time taken by different groups to simplify efficiency calculations.

questions.question: Total length of train A and train B is 600 metres. These trains are running in opposite direction. Total speed of train A and train B is 40 m/s. In how much time (in seconds) these trains will cross each other?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For trains crossing each other in **opposite direction**, the **Relative Speed** is the sum of their individual speeds.

**Total distance** to be covered = Sum of **lengths** of both trains = 600 m.

**Relative Speed** = 40 m/s (given as total speed).

**Time** = Distance ÷ Speed = 600 ÷ 40 = 15 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **length** of Train A and Train B (LA + LB) = 600 m

Total **speed** (Relative Speed in opposite direction) = 40 m/s

**Formula Used:**

Time = (Sum of Lengths of Trains) ÷ (Relative Speed)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/195ccb90d54ad3cc0bde8d8286492e5f9dd532ddd355050a0d66cc5400f24452.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Distance** = 600 m

⇒ **Relative Speed** = 40 m/s

⇒ **Time** = 600 ÷ 40

⇒ **Time** = 15 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 15 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. When they move in the **same direction**, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Crossing Conditions

To cross a stationary pole or man, distance = **Length of Train**. To cross a platform or another train, distance = **Length of Train + Length of Object**.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: A started from point P to reach point Q at the speed of 50 km/hr. At the same time, B started from point Q to reach point P at the speed of 30 km/hr. They met in between at point S. What is the ratio of distances covered by A and B to reach point S?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two objects start at the **same time** and move towards each other, the **time** (t) taken to meet is **constant** for both.

Since **Distance = Speed × Time**, when time is constant, **Distance ∝ Speed**.

∴ Ratio of distances covered by A and B = Ratio of their speeds = **50 : 30**.

Simplified Ratio = **5 : 3**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Speed of A = **50 km/hr**, Speed of B = **30 km/hr**. Both start simultaneously.

**Formula Used:** Distance = **Speed × Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/116ddb630307f30d1f4cb8f1775da04d1156221475770f51c932ef7bf7ceb270.png] 

⇒ Let the time taken by both A and B to meet at point **S** be **t** hours.

⇒ Distance covered by A to reach S = **PS** = SpeedA × t = **50t**

⇒ Distance covered by B to reach S = **QS** = SpeedB × t = **30t**

⇒ Ratio of distances covered = **PS : QS**

⇒ Ratio = 50t : 30t

⇒ Ratio = 50 : 30 = **5 : 3**

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, their **Relative Speed** is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Constant Distance Relation

If the **distance** is constant, the ratio of speeds is **inversely proportional** to the ratio of time taken (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Meeting Time Formula

Time taken to meet = **Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed**. This applies when both start at the same time.
